chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rib'i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked him, 'If a man lags behind while he is in prayer, is it permissible?' He said, 'No.' I asked, 'And if he advances?' He said, 'Yes, walking towards the Qibla.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to walk forward or backward during congregational prayer to adjust one's position?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the fiqh of congregational alignment by permitting a worshipper to advance to the front of the row while walking towards the Qibla, while generally discouraging lagging behind. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining orderly rows (saff) and the physical act of joining the collective worship as an expression of unity and humility before God.
